problem: The text says every block group carries a copy of the superblock and group descriptors. On a default ext2 file system (sparse_super) only group 0, group 1 and groups whose number is a power of 3, 5 or 7 keep backups; the other groups start straight at the bitmaps.
fix: Write: each group has its own block bitmap, inode bitmap, inode table and data blocks, and some groups also hold a backup copy of the superblock and group descriptors.

where: Figure caption and aria text of the ext2 block diagram
problem: "the inode table pointing into data blocks" and "the inode table ... holds the block pointers" make the table itself the pointer holder. The inodes inside the table hold the 15 block pointers.
fix: Say: each inode record inside the inode table holds the 15 block pointers that lead to data blocks.

problem: The vertical chain puts a boot block at the top of the per-group sequence, which suggests every block group begins with a boot block. The 1 KB boot block exists only once, at the start of the file system (block 0).
fix: Label the diagram as group 0 or note that the boot block appears only at the start of the file system; later groups begin with the superblock backup (where one exists), then the bitmaps and inode table.

problem: The arithmetic shown is (300000 − 274432) ÷ 1024 = 24.9, but 25568 ÷ 1024 = 24.97, and the block index comes from taking the floor, which the answer does not state.
fix: answer: Direct ends at 12287, single at 274431, so double indirect; (300000 − 274432) ÷ 1024 = 25568 ÷ 1024 = 24.97, and floor gives block index 24.

problem: 16,843,020 KB (about 16.06 GiB) is the capacity of the pointer scheme, but it is presented as the largest ext2 file. An ext2 inode stores the size in a 32-bit field, so a real ext2 file is capped at 4 GiB, well below the counted value. As written, a student will quote 16 GiB as the ext2 file-size limit.
fix: Keep the count but label it: the 15 pointers can address 16843020 blocks = 16843020 KB ≈ 16.06 GiB; an actual ext2 file is limited below this by the 32-bit size field in the inode (4 GiB).
